title: 3D Volumetric Data Heatmap (Slice Planes)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a procedurally generated 32×32×32 scalar volume dataset, and display it in pseudocolor using multiple slice planes.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Volume Data]
(1) Procedurally generate a 32³ float volume: the primary structure must be a Gaussian blob with a small amount of noise.
(2) Include at least three orthogonal slice planes: XY, XZ, and YZ (PlaneGeometry + DataTexture or a shader sampling a 3D texture may be used).
(3) id="sliceX", id="sliceY", and id="sliceZ": range sliders control the position of each slice in voxel index space (0–31 or normalized 0–1; the positions must be reflected in __3D_STATE__.slicePositions).
(4) id="threshold": a threshold slider; fragments below/above the threshold must be transparent or hidden (transfer function).
(5) id="colormap": a select element for switching the colormap (for example, several named strings such as viridis / hot / cool).

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  volumeSize: number,
  slicePositions: { x: number, y: number, z: number },
  threshold: number,
  colormap: string,
  maxValue: number,
  minValue: number
}

volumeSize must be 32; minValue <= maxValue, and both must be finite numbers.

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
physics_constraints: XY/XZ/YZ slice planes with sliders sliceX sliceY sliceZ
